extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, in-house counsel, and district court judges handling patent cases
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural best-practice guidance for conducting claim construction (Markman) and Festo equivalents issues together with summary judgment on infringement early in patent litigation, with a targeted discovery plan and pre-hearing procedures. The goal is to enable dispositive resolution of infringement/scope issues before broad fact discovery (damages, willfulness, validity) proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction: ordinary and customary meaning; specification as guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims are interpreted as they would be understood by 'one of ordinary skill in the art' — words are generally given their ordinary and customary meaning; the specification is 'the single best guide' to the meaning of a disputed claim term; a patentee may be his own lexicographer if a special definition is clearly stated in the specification or file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts first look at the words of the claims and the specification; review the specification to determine whether the inventor used terms inconsistently with ordinary meaning. If the intrinsic evidence resolves the meaning, it is improper to rely on extrinsic evidence to change that meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of intrinsic evidence over extrinsic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Intrinsic evidence (claims, specification, prosecution history) is 'the most significant source of the legally operative meaning of disputed claim language' and should be consulted first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extrinsic evidence (expert testimony, dictionaries, treatises, scientific articles) may be considered to help understand the technology but 'may not be used to vary or contradict claim language.' If intrinsic record is sufficient, extrinsic evidence should be excluded as contrary to precedent (citing Vitronics and Markman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dictionaries, encyclopedias and treatises as aids to ordinary meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may consult dictionaries, encyclopedias and treatises to ascertain possible meanings that would have been attributed to claim words by those skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references are unbiased reflections of common understanding and 'entirely proper' to consult at any litigation stage; use them to identify possible meanings and then use intrinsic record to select the meaning most consistent with the inventor's use (per Texas Digital).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution history estoppel and Festo standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution history is relevant to literal meaning and to the scope of equivalents; amendments made during prosecution may create a rebuttable presumption that narrower scope was surrendered (Festo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A narrowing amendment triggers a presumption of surrender unless patentee shows at the time of amendment one skilled in the art could not reasonably have drafted a claim to encompass the equivalent. An amendment does not surrender an equivalent if (1) the equivalent was unforeseeable at application time; (2) the rationale for amendment is only tangential to the equivalent; or (3) other reasons suggest the patentee could not reasonably have been expected to describe the equivalent. The patentee bears the burden to rebut the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an early combined Markman/Festo hearing with summary judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where feasible, combine claim construction and equivalents (Markman/Festo) in a single early hearing together with summary judgment motions on infringement ('summary judgment trial') before extensive fact discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: claim scope and infringement often decide the case and resolving them early can avoid millions in irrelevant discovery costs (damages, willfulness, broad invalidity searches). The combined hearing should permit targeted discovery limited to matters relevant to claim construction and infringement and may include live testimony, opening/closing, cross-examination, and dispositive summary judgment rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of document production for an early Markman/summary judgment phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Document production for the initial round should be targeted and not open-ended, focusing on materials relevant to claim construction and infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested documents the patentee should produce: (1) all documents relating to patent prosecution from initial disclosure through issuance; (2) documents relating to inventors' conception and reduction to practice; (3) documents in the relevant technology area that use any claim term at issue; (4) documents discussing the patent or application (including marking); (5) documents adequate to show operation or design of any product the patentee contends is covered. Suggested documents the accused infringer should produce: (1) documents adequate to show operation or design of accused products; (2) documents reflecting accused infringer's knowledge of the patent-in-suit; (3) documents in the relevant technology area using any disputed claim term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions appropriate for the early phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit depositions in the initial phase to fact witnesses whose testimony is relevant to claim construction and infringement rather than broad roving fact discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate depositions include a Rule 30(b)(6) witness to discuss operation of accused products, inventor depositions, possibly the prosecuting attorney (where relevant), fact witnesses who produced responsive documents, and expert witness depositions. Avoid numerous marginal witnesses who have not read the patent and whose testimony invites 'legal conclusion' objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-hearing procedures: simultaneous exchange, meet-and-confer, expert reports, and timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a structured pre-hearing process to narrow claim term disputes and prepare for the combined hearing: simultaneous exchange of proposed claim term definitions (without prejudice), meet-and-confer to narrow issues, exchange of briefs and expert reports, rebuttals, expert depositions, then the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include: (1) exchange lists of claim terms with proposed definitions (inadmissible/without prejudice); (2) meet and confer and memorialize agreements; (3) exchange claim construction briefs and serve expert reports under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2) addressing claim construction and infringement; (4) serve rebuttal briefs and rebuttal expert reports; (5) take expert depositions; (6) hold Markman hearing combined with summary judgment motions. This simultaneous-exchange approach encourages narrowing and avoids tactical prejudice from interim concessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markman/Festo hearing format and effect ('summary judgment trial')
rubrics_metrics.description: A combined hearing can be conducted with features of a trial (opening, closing, live testimony, cross-examination) and may be dispositive via summary judgment, though technically the court's role is to construe claims as a matter of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a Markman decision is a legal determination, in practice judges hearing live testimony may make credibility determinations and weight evidence — the proceeding may therefore have trial-like attributes. If the court grants summary judgment of non-infringement the case can end; if not, remaining issues (willfulness, damages, validity) proceed to discovery and jury trial as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards and expert evidence in claim construction hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Rules of Evidence govern court proceedings generally, but courts often admit extrinsic evidence (expert testimony, tutorials, treatises) to educate the court; Daubert gatekeeping principles apply to expert testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daubert factors (testability, peer review, known error rates, general acceptance) guide admissibility and reliability of expert testimony; Kumho Tire extends Daubert to technical expertise. Courts frequently admit expert testimony as background to assist interpretation of claim language, and judges may consult treatises/dictionaries on their own. Parties should be prepared to raise evidentiary objections and to move to strike exhibits or seek in limine rulings where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel strategy and risks in early claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must clearly articulate their proposed claim scope early; patentees advocating broad constructions risk invalidity if the construction reads on prior art, while accused infringers benefit from early resolution to focus validity/design-around efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early construction reduces the problem of 'moving' claim constructions that change as new prior art or arguments appear. The proposal suggests that the patent owner bears the risk of pushing an expansive construction that later renders the patent invalid; defendants gain efficiency by knowing the claim scope early and concentrating subsequent discovery/trial strategy accordingly.
